Question Choices: What are "buckets" in a histogram?  (A) The tallest bars in the graph.    (B) The total number of data points.   (C) Groups or intervals of data values
Hints: Distinguish an interval of values from its frequency.
Solution: A histogram divides numerical values into non-overlapping intervals (bins or buckets), then shows how many observations lie in each interval. It does not retain each exact observation.

Question Choices: A histogram shows screen time: Class A has 4 students at 2-3 hours and 3 at 3-4 hours; Class B has 6 at 2-3 hours and 5 at 3-4 hours. Which class has more students with 2 or more hours of screen time? These are all bins at or above2 hours; bins include their lower endpoint.
Hints: Sum the two stated frequencies for each class.
Solution: Class A:4+3=7. Class B:6+5=11. Since11>7, choose B.

Question Choices: In Class B, 8 students are in the 2-3 bucket and 5 students are in the 1-2 bucket. How many more students are in 2-3 than 1-2?
Hints: Read the relevant counts, then add or subtract as requested.
Solution: Use frequencies (numbers of observations), not interval labels. Combine the relevant frequencies: 8-5=3.

Question Choices: A histogram has buckets 0-29 with 3 values, 30-59 with 9 values, and 60-89 with 5 values. Which statement is correct? (A) Most data is in 0-29.   (B) Most data is in 30-59   (C) All buckets are equal
Solution: There are3+9+5=17 observations. Nine lie in30–59, which is the largest group and exceeds half of17, so B.
